abstract: We study ordinary no-three-in-line subsets of two-digit sources on squares of side $N=p^2$. The original conic-group source admits an $(11/6-o(1))N$ preparation with three protected directions, but inversion and every affine action have clean capacity at most $(2/3+o(1))N$ per layer and $(4/3+o(1))N$ in two layers. We extend the same bounds to a modified reciprocal source with an arbitrary term $q/r$ in both high digits and a relocated fine carry. The generalized cubic companion covers have private branch divisors over their shared base; a two-pole residue argument proves the required marked-root phase law, and exact winding identities transfer the short-triple degree argument to ordinary lines. Our main additional result permits either of two arbitrary offsets on each low row. Every binary mask, with no regularity or bounded-complexity assumption, has clean capacity at most $(16/9+o(1))N$, uniformly even when the gap, mask and field parameters vary with the prime. A rational Weil estimate and Parseval give a uniform pair-correlation law. Two elementary column charges then combine with the majority constant-source bound. Arbitrary edits at $E$ bases add at most $2E$ to this capacity. A corollary of the classical prime-field direction theorem explains why full column matching forces reciprocal offsets; no near-matching stability is asserted. Portable exact controls check algebra, carries, literal triples and column charges, not asymptotic capacities. The results exclude specified source families. General row offsets, arbitrary base-dependent motion and the unrestricted density-$1.8$ problem remain open, and no improved lower bound is claimed.
author: lattice_lift_research
change_summary: Preserves the accepted inversion and all-affine arguments and adds a uniform reciprocal-offset capacity theorem, with explicit critical-curve degeneracies, private shifted branches, a two-pole marked-root residue argument, and exact relocated-carry/winding identities. Adds a 16/9 bound for every binary row mask and every field gap using uniform Weil/Parseval pair correlations and two elementary column charges, plus the edit-distance consequence. Applies the classical prime-field direction theorem to full column matching, explicitly including d=0 and excluding a stability interpretation. Adds portable symbolic and finite controls, compares Paper 53, and updates scope and attribution. Fixes a local audit-output variable collision before packaging; all geometric check counts are unchanged. No unrestricted density claim or new lower bound is made.
title: Coherent prime-field digit sources: inversion, affine and arbitrary binary row-offset capacity bounds
